title: Pass untrusted issue text into workflow shell steps through env, not inline expressions
answers: workflow script injection from issue title
how to use issue title in a GitHub Actions run step safely
why is the issue title assigned to an env variable in triage workflow
body:
Convention: user-controlled event fields (issue title, body) are passed to a `run:` step via `env:` and read as shell variables (`TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}` then `"${TITLE}"`), not interpolated directly as `${{ github.event.issue.title }}` inside the script text.
Enforced by: .github/workflows/triage.yml:jobs.label.steps (the env block feeding the title-matching script).
Inline interpolation would let a crafted issue title inject shell commands into the runner, since the expression is substituted before bash parses the script.
Matching is done in pure bash with no LLM or external service: leading whitespace is trimmed and the title is upper-cased with `${title^^}` before `case` prefix matching, and unmatched titles exit 0 without changes.
Reuse this pattern for any new workflow that reads issue or PR text.
applies: Any GitHub Actions workflow in this repo whose run steps read issue or PR titles or bodies.
says: Submitting an issue with quotes or special characters causes workflow script injection
Malicious issue titles can execute unauthorized shell commands during automated issue triage
Prevent crafted issue or pull request titles from injecting commands into automation
Automated triage workflow fails when processing issue titles that contain shell characters
search: In GitHub Actions run steps, untrusted issue and pull request titles or bodies must be passed via env variables rather than interpolated directly into script text. Enforced in .github/workflows/triage.yml:jobs.label.steps by mapping ${{ github.event.issue.title }} to an env variable, this convention prevents crafted issue titles from injecting shell commands into the runner. Title matching is handled in pure bash by trimming whitespace and uppercasing with ${title^^} for case matching, exiting 0 on unmatched titles without external services.
